subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should reset-archive recovery be solved by a mutable restore/re-index flow, the open opt-in read-only family-history API, or both under a Doctor/recovery UX?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent contract changes how archived transcripts are exposed to models/tools and whether OpenClaw mutates historical transcript files or session indexes during recovery.

options.title: Prefer Read-Only Family History First
options.body: Review and land the bounded `includeFamily` path, then decide whether a separate restore/re-index command is still needed for already-affected users.

options.title: Build Doctor Restore/Re-Index
options.body: Add an explicit recovery command or UI/Doctor path that backs up state, renames or imports selected archives, rebuilds indexes, and warns about retention.

options.title: Keep Mutable Restore Out Of Core
options.body: Treat archive restoration as external/manual tooling while keeping core focused on read-only discovery and explicit history retrieval.

recommendation.title: Prefer Read-Only Family History First
recommendation.body: Review and land the bounded `includeFamily` path, then decide whether a separate restore/re-index command is still needed for already-affected users.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to the session/gateway helper surfaces where the permanent recovery contract would land.
